1	# Structural BPMN (what the registry does not emit)
2	
3	The registry's `xmlTemplate`s give you the `uipath:*` payload for each node
4	(see [registry-workflow.md](registry-workflow.md)). They do **not** give you the
5	structural BPMN that holds those nodes together. This file is the ground truth
6	for everything you author by hand around the templates.
7	
8	Two sources define the contract:
9	
10	- the registry spec `bpmn-spec.json` — enumerates which BPMN element types and
11	  event definitions exist, via its `bpmnElements` section;
12	- the Studio Web canvas serializer
13	  (`PO.Frontend/src/services/serialization/`) — defines how that XML must be
14	  shaped to import and round-trip.
15	
16	Where the registry stops, the canvas serializer is authoritative. Each
17	gap below is labelled **REGISTRY GAP** — the registry exposes no template for
18	it, so author it from this reference.
19	
20	## The document scaffold (REGISTRY GAP)
21	
22	The registry emits no `<bpmn:definitions>` / `<bpmn:process>` root and no
23	namespace declarations. Author this shell yourself. The canvas import detector
24	(`exporter.ts`) requires: a root `<…:definitions>` carrying a BPMN-spec
25	namespace, at least one `<bpmn:process>`, and (to render) a
26	`<bpmndi:BPMNDiagram>`.

28	```xml

133	## Variables (`BPMN.Variables`)
134	
135	Declare root variables with the `BPMN.Variables` registry template attached to
136	the process via `extensionElements`, or use the canvas `<uipath:variables>`
137	block directly. Variable bodies are CDATA. Reference variables in expressions as
138	`vars.<id>` — see [expression-authoring.md](expression-authoring.md).
139	Sub-process-scoped variables go in that sub-process's own `<uipath:variables>`.
140	
141	## Script tasks (`BPMN.ScriptTask`) — Jint runtime contract
142	
143	`bpmn:scriptTask scriptFormat="JavaScript"` runs under **Jint**, not Node.js or
144	a browser. The mapping payload comes from the `BPMN.ScriptTask` registry
145	template, but the runtime contract is fixed:
146	
147	- Only these helpers exist: `uipath.aggregate`, `uipath._aggregate`,
148	  `uipath._pipe`, and a no-op `console`. No npm packages, filesystem, network,
149	  browser globals, or long-running async behavior. Execution envelope is ~64 MB
150	  / 30 s.
151	- Set `uipath:scriptVersion value="v3"` for new scripts; preserve an imported
152	  `value="v2"`. For v2+ the script returns JSON under `response`.
153	- Mapped `args` fields are read as **top-level identifiers** in the script body
154	  (`amount`, not `args.amount`); the input mapping itself stays `name="args"`
155	  and maps each field by variable id (`=vars.Var_Amount`).
156	- Map the return back through `source="=result.response"` (scalar) or
157	  `source="=result.response.<field>"` (object field); `var` points at a declared
158	  variable id (do not put the target id in `name`).
159	- Do not mutate `Globals.*`, `vars.*`, or process variables inside the script
160	  body. The supported path is: return a value from the script, then use a
161	  `uipath:output` mapping to write it to the declared variable. Direct mutation
162	  is not applied to the runtime, so the variable reads empty afterward.
163	
164	```xml
165	<bpmn:scriptTask id="Task_RiskScore" name="Risk Score" scriptFormat="JavaScript">
166	  <bpmn:extensionElements>
167	    <uipath:scriptVersion value="v3" />
168	    <uipath:mapping version="v1">
169	      <uipath:type value="BPMN.ScriptTask" version="v1" />
170	      <uipath:input name="args"><![CDATA[{"amount":"=vars.Var_Amount","daysOverdue":"=vars.Var_DaysOverdue"}]]></uipath:input>
171	      <uipath:output name="riskScore" type="number" var="Var_RiskScore" source="=result.response" />
172	    </uipath:mapping>
173	  </bpmn:extensionElements>
174	  <bpmn:script><![CDATA[
175	var score = amount * 0.01 + daysOverdue * 2;
176	return { response: score };
177	]]></bpmn:script>
178	</bpmn:scriptTask>
179	```
180	
181	## Sequence flows, conditions, and gateway defaults (REGISTRY GAP)
182	
183	The registry never emits `<bpmn:sequenceFlow>`, conditions, or the gateway
184	`default` attribute. Author all of them.
185	
186	- A flow: `<bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_1" sourceRef="A" targetRef="B" />`. The
187	  source/target nodes must also list `<bpmn:incoming>`/`<bpmn:outgoing>`
188	  (the registry templates leave `{incomingEdge}`/`{outgoingEdge}` placeholders
189	  for exactly these).
190	- Conditional flow body: `<bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">=vars.Var_X == "approved"</bpmn:conditionExpression>`.
191	  The canvas normalizes the body to start with `=` — always lead with `=`.
192	- Gateway default flow: set `default="Flow_else"` on the gateway element, and
193	  give that flow no condition.
194	
195	## Gateways
196	
197	Author these gateway types for new BPMN: `bpmn:ExclusiveGateway`,
198	`bpmn:ParallelGateway`, `bpmn:InclusiveGateway`, `bpmn:EventBasedGateway`.
199	`bpmn:ComplexGateway` round-trips structurally but is **preserve-only** — do not
200	generate it for new authoring (see [Do not generate for new
201	authoring](#do-not-generate-for-new-authoring-preserve-on-round-trip-only)).
202	
203	- **Exclusive (XOR)**: each non-default outgoing flow needs a
204	  `conditionExpression`; exactly one outgoing flow is the `default`. (Validator
205	  rule `MISSING_CONDITION_EXPRESSION`.)
206	- **Parallel (AND)**: fork = one in, many out; join = many in, one out. No
207	  conditions.
208	- **Inclusive (OR)**: conditions on outgoing flows; multiple may be taken.
209	- **Event-based**: routes to the first of several catch events / receive tasks
210	  to fire; its outgoing flows target intermediate catch events or receive tasks.
211	- A gateway with exactly one incoming and one outgoing flow is rejected
212	  (`SUPERFLUOUS_GATEWAY`). Activities/events must not have more than one
213	  incoming flow — join with a gateway, not a "fake join" (`FAKE_JOIN`).
214	
215	## Events and the event-definition matrix
216	
217	`bpmn-spec.json` `bpmnElements.events` enumerates which event definitions each
218	event element can carry on **round-trip**. For **new authoring**, only the
219	**none**, **Message**, **Timer**, **Error** (on end + boundary), and
220	**Terminate** (on end events only) definitions are generated. Conditional,
221	Signal, Escalation, Compensate, Cancel, Link, multiple, and parallel-multiple
222	definitions are **preserve-only** — keep them when imported, but do not generate
223	them for new BPMN (see [Do not generate for new
224	authoring](#do-not-generate-for-new-authoring-preserve-on-round-trip-only)).
225	
226	The matrix below is the round-trip acceptance per element; **preserve-only**
227	marks definitions that the skill keeps but does not author for new files.
228	
229	| Event element | Authorable | Preserve-only (round-trip) |
230	| --- | --- | --- |
231	| `bpmn:StartEvent` | none, Message, Timer | Conditional, Signal |
232	| `bpmn:IntermediateThrowEvent` | none, Message | Escalation, Signal, Link, Compensate |
233	| `bpmn:IntermediateCatchEvent` | Message, Timer | Escalation, Signal, Conditional, Link, Compensate |
234	| `bpmn:EndEvent` | none, Message, Error, Terminate | Escalation, Compensate, Signal |
235	| `bpmn:BoundaryEvent` | Message, Timer, Error | Escalation, Conditional, Signal, Compensate |
236	
237	Payload shapes the canvas serializes:
238	
239	- **Timer**: `<bpmn:timerEventDefinition><bpmn:timeDuration xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">PT30M</bpmn:timeDuration></bpmn:timerEventDefinition>`
240	  (or `timeDate` / `timeCycle`). Static durations must be valid ISO-8601;
241	  week designators (`PnW`) are unsupported. Expression-mode is allowed and
242	  accepts either prefix — `=…` or `@…`.
243	- **Message**: `<bpmn:messageEventDefinition messageRef="Message_1" />` with a
244	  `<bpmn:message id="Message_1" name="…"/>` declared at definitions level. The
245	  Maestro internal-message events (`Maestro.ReceiveMessageEvent` /
246	  `Maestro.SendMessageEvent`) carry the `uipath:event` payload **and** a bare
247	  `<bpmn:messageEventDefinition />` (see their registry templates).
248	- **Error**: `<bpmn:errorEventDefinition errorRef="Error_1" />` with a
249	  `<bpmn:error id="Error_1" name="…" errorCode="…"/>` at definitions level. An
250	  error end event with no `errorRef` fails to parse at runtime
251	  (`ERROR_END_EVENT_MISSING_EXCEPTION`); an error referenced by a boundary event
252	  must declare an `errorCode` (`ERROR_BOUNDARY_EVENT_REQUIRES_ERROR_CODE`).
253	- **Terminate** (end events only): emit the bare
254	  `<bpmn:terminateEventDefinition />`.
255	
256	Preserve-only payloads — keep these when imported, but do not author them for
257	new files:
258	
259	- **Signal**: `<bpmn:signalEventDefinition signalRef="Signal_1" />` with a
260	  definitions-level `<bpmn:signal/>`.
261	- **Escalation**: `<bpmn:escalationEventDefinition escalationRef="Escalation_1" />`
262	  with a `<bpmn:escalation id="Escalation_1" name="…" escalationCode="…"/>`
263	  declared at definitions level (parallel to message/error/signal).
264	- **Conditional / Link / Compensate**: the bare definition element; the canvas
265	  round-trips it.
266	
267	### Boundary events (REGISTRY GAP for `attachedToRef` / `cancelActivity`)
268	
269	A boundary event attaches to an activity and catches an event on it. The
270	registry exposes no boundary template; author it:
271	
272	```xml
273	<bpmn:boundaryEvent id="Boundary_Timeout" attachedToRef="Task_DoWork" cancelActivity="true">
274	  <bpmn:timerEventDefinition>
275	    <bpmn:timeDuration xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">PT15M</bpmn:timeDuration>
276	  </bpmn:timerEventDefinition>
277	  <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_OnTimeout</bpmn:outgoing>
278	</bpmn:boundaryEvent>
279	```
280	
281	- `attachedToRef` = id of the activity it sits on. The boundary event and that
282	  activity must be `flowElements` of the same parent scope.
283	- `cancelActivity="true"` = interrupting (default); `cancelActivity="false"` =
284	  non-interrupting. Per the spec, non-interrupting is available for
285	  Message/Timer/Escalation/Conditional/Signal — **not** Error or Compensate.
286	- Only one catch-all (no `errorRef`) error boundary event per task, and no two
287	  error boundary events with the same error code on one task
288	  (`MULTIPLE_CATCH_ALL_BOUNDARY_EVENTS_ON_TASK`,
289	  `DUPLICATE_ERROR_BOUNDARY_EVENT_ON_TASK`).
290	
291	### Retry and error mapping (REGISTRY GAP)
292	
293	UiPath-specific retry and error-mapping metadata live inside an activity's
294	`extensionElements`. The error **code** lives on the declared
295	`bpmn:error errorCode="…"`; `uipath:*` elements reference it through `errorRef`.
296	
297	```xml
298	<uipath:retry maxRetryCount="2" retryBackoff="PT30S" retryBackoffType="exponential"
299	              maxDuration="PT5M" exponentialBase="2" retryAllErrors="false">
300	  <uipath:errorDefinition errorRef="Error_ServiceUnavailable" />
301	</uipath:retry>
302	<uipath:errorMapping version="v1">
303	  <uipath:error id="Mapped_ServiceUnavailable" errorRef="Error_ServiceUnavailable"
304	                priority="1" condition="=vars.error.code == "SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE""
305	                detail="Service unavailable" retryable="true" />
306	</uipath:errorMapping>
307	```
308	
309	- `uipath:retry` attributes: `maxRetryCount`, `retryBackoff`, `retryBackoffType`,
310	  `maxDuration`, `exponentialBase`, `retryAllErrors`. Do not use stale aliases
311	  (`maxAttempts`, `interval`).
312	- `uipath:error` (mapping) fields: `id`, `errorRef`, `priority`, `condition`,
313	  `detail`, `retryable` (`true`/`false`). Conditions read the runtime error via
314	  `vars.error` and contain no assignments. Do not put `code=` on `uipath:error`;
315	  model the code on `bpmn:error errorCode` and reference via `errorRef`.
316	
317	## Subprocess, call activity, event subprocess (REGISTRY GAP for structure)
318	
319	- **SubProcess** (`bpmn:SubProcess`): a container with its own nested
320	  `flowElements` (start event, nodes, end event) and its own scoped
321	  `<uipath:variables>`. Variants: `collapsed`, `expanded`, `eventSubprocess`.
322	  The shape carries `isExpanded` for the collapsed/expanded distinction.
323	- **Event subprocess**: a `bpmn:SubProcess` with `triggeredByEvent="true"`. It
324	  must have **exactly one** start event, and that start event **must carry an
325	  event definition** (with `isInterrupting`) — a blank start event is invalid for
326	  an event subprocess.
327	- **Call activity** (`bpmn:CallActivity`): invokes a *separate* Maestro
328	  instance. The registry provides the `uipath:activity` payload for the
329	  Orchestrator agentic/case-management call-activity types
330	  (`Orchestrator.StartAgenticProcess[Async]`, `…CaseMgmtProcess[Async]`). A
331	  plain BPMN `calledElement` round-trips but is not specially authored by the
332	  canvas layer.
333	- Each scope (process or sub-process) may have at most one blank (untyped) start
334	  event (`MULTIPLE_BLANK_START_EVENTS`).
335	
336	> SubProcess scopes operations *within the same instance*; CallActivity invokes
337	> a *separate* Maestro instance. Do not conflate them.
338	
339	## Multi-instance / loop characteristics (REGISTRY GAP — canvas supports it)
340	
341	The registry spec enumerates **no** multi-instance or loop markers
342	(`grep` for `multiInstance`/`loopCharacteristics` in `bpmn-spec.json` returns
343	nothing). This is a genuine registry gap. The Studio Web canvas, however, **does**
344	serialize them (`elements/nodes.ts`), so author them from the canvas contract:
345	
346	```xml
347	<bpmn:multiInstanceLoopCharacteristics isSequential="true">
348	  <bpmn:completionCondition xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">=vars.Var_Done</bpmn:completionCondition>
349	  <bpmn:extensionElements>
350	    <uipath:loopCharacteristics
351	        inputCollection="=vars.Var_Items" inputElement="item" />
352	  </bpmn:extensionElements>
353	</bpmn:multiInstanceLoopCharacteristics>
354	```
355	
356	- `isSequential="true"` = one at a time; `false` = parallel.
357	- The collection/item binding lives in the `uipath:loopCharacteristics`
358	  extension (`inputCollection`, `inputElement`), **not** in `loopCardinality`
359	  (the canvas never reads `loopCardinality`).
360	- The loop element **must declare `inputElement`** — do not rely on reading a
361	  bare `iterator`/`iterator.item` downstream without it. For a multi-instance
362	  **subprocess** body, bind `inputElement="iterator[0]"` on
363	  `uipath:loopCharacteristics` and pass the current item into body activities
364	  with `=iterator[0].item`. Do not assume a bare alias such as `=currentItem` is
365	  in scope inside a marker subprocess body unless the file already uses it.
366	- Inside the body, read the current item with the `iterator` namespace — see
367	  [expression-authoring.md](expression-authoring.md).
368	- `bpmn:standardLoopCharacteristics` is also recognized (no uipath extension).
369	
370	Because the registry exposes no template for this, treat it as a documented
371	authoring path backed by the canvas serializer, and tell the user it is a
372	registry gap if they ask why no `registry get` covers it.
373	
374	## Do not generate for new authoring (preserve on round-trip only)
375	
376	These structures are **not** authored for new Maestro BPMN. If they appear in an
377	imported or brownfield file, preserve them and report that the skill cannot
378	safely regenerate or normalize them. Planned / preview / TBD statuses count as
379	unsupported for generation until current tooling confirms them.
380	
381	- Gateway: `bpmn:complexGateway`.
382	- Tasks / containers: `bpmn:manualTask`, `bpmn:adHocSubProcess`,
383	  `bpmn:transaction`.
384	- Event definitions: `conditionalEventDefinition`, `signalEventDefinition`,
385	  `escalationEventDefinition`, `compensateEventDefinition`,
386	  `cancelEventDefinition`, `linkEventDefinition`, multiple, and
387	  parallel-multiple event definitions.
388	- Markers: standard-loop and compensation markers (use only documented
389	  multi-instance parallel/sequential metadata for new loops).
390	- Terminate is supported **only** on end events — not on start, boundary,
391	  intermediate-catch, or intermediate-throw events.
392	- Preserve-only `uipath:*` extension payloads: keep these when imported, and when
393	  a file legitimately needs one, reproduce the shape (with synthetic, public-safe
394	  contents) rather than inventing a new one.
395	  - **Typed activity/event shells always use the lowercase `<uipath:activity>` /
396	    `<uipath:event>` wrapper with a `<uipath:type value="<Type>" version="v1" />`
397	    child** — including types not served by the live registry (e.g.
398	    `Maestro.CasePlanScheduler`, `Maestro.CaseManagerGuardrails`,
399	    `Maestro.CaseRulesEvaluator`). Do **not** substitute the capital-`A`
400	    `<uipath:Activity>` element for a typed shell.
401	  - The capital-`A` `<uipath:Activity>` element is a **separate** generic
402	    preserve-only payload (its own element, not a wrapper for typed shells).
403	  - `uipath:caseManagement` is a versioned body-string element —
404	    `<uipath:caseManagement version="v1">…synthetic payload…</uipath:caseManagement>`.
405	  - `<uipath:scriptVersion value="v2" />` is legacy: author `v3` for new scripts,
406	    preserve `v2` where it already exists.
407	
408	## Diagram interchange — `bpmndi` (REGISTRY GAP — always generated)
409	
410	The registry emits no diagram. Import is **diagram-driven**: the canvas builds
411	nodes from `BPMNShape`s and edges from `BPMNEdge`s, not by walking
412	`flowElements`. **A node with no shape is invisible; a flow with no edge is
413	dropped.** You must generate the full `BPMNDiagram` yourself.
414	
415	- One `<bpmndi:BPMNShape id="S_<nodeId>" bpmnElement="<nodeId>">` per node, with
416	  `<dc:Bounds x= y= width= height= />`. SubProcess shapes carry `isExpanded`.
417	- One `<bpmndi:BPMNEdge id="BPMNEdge_<flowId>" bpmnElement="<flowId>">` per
418	  sequence flow, with `<di:waypoint x= y= />` points.
419	- Lay nodes out left-to-right with non-overlapping bounds. Typical sizes: tasks
420	  100×80, events 36×36, gateways 50×50.
421	
422	Example:
423	
424	```xml
425	<bpmndi:BPMNShape id="S_StartEvent_1" bpmnElement="StartEvent_1">
426	  <dc:Bounds x="160" y="100" width="36" height="36" />
427	</bpmndi:BPMNShape>
428	<bpmndi:BPMNEdge id="BPMNEdge_Flow_1" bpmnElement="Flow_1">
429	  <di:waypoint x="196" y="118" />
430	  <di:waypoint x="260" y="118" />
431	</bpmndi:BPMNEdge>
432	```
433	
434	## Editing operations
435	
436	Safe, surgical edits on an existing `.bpmn` (preserve content you did not author
437	— see [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#editing-an-existing-bpmn-preserve-what-you-did-not-author)):
438	
439	- **Add / delete / reconnect a node**: add the element with a stable id and its
440	  `<bpmn:incoming>`/`<bpmn:outgoing>` refs, add the sequence-flow elements in the
441	  owning scope, and add/update its `BPMNShape` and edge waypoints. On delete,
442	  remove orphaned flows and DI edges and recheck entry-point variables, output
443	  mappings, and binding references.
444	- **Insert a gateway**: split the existing sequence flow into an incoming and an
445	  outgoing flow, add conditions to the outgoing flows plus one `default`, add a
446	  matching join only if branches actually need synchronization, then re-waypoint
447	  the diagram (gateway shape + all edges).
448	- **Move logic into a subprocess**: move only elements that share a valid scope,
449	  re-scope their variables, recreate legal subprocess flow boundaries, and add a
450	  second diagram plane for the subprocess so nested content renders.
451	- **Add an entry point**: use a root-level start event, add a stable unique
452	  `uipath:entryPointId`, and declare input/output variables whose `elementId`
453	  matches that start event.
454	
455	Do not patch generated JSON to fix source behavior — change the `.bpmn` and
456	regenerate. For `Intsvc.*` activities/triggers, hand editing to CLI enrichment.
457	
458	### Edit red-flags
459	
460	Re-check after any edit:
461	
462	- A diagram plane references a missing process, collaboration, or subprocess.
463	- A rendered element lacks a shape or its flow lacks an edge/waypoint.
464	- An entry-point variable points at the wrong start event.
465	- A `uipath:context` value references a missing binding.
466	- A topology edit rewrote unrelated `uipath:*` extension XML.
467	- An Integration Service element carries hand-authored connection details.
468	
469	## Validation
470	
471	There is **no** `uip maestro bpmn validate` CLI command. The skill ships its own
472	offline validator that reconstructs the PO.Frontend Node/Edge/CanvasState model
473	from the parsed BPMN and runs **every** canvas validation rule — run it as the
474	primary check:
475	
476	```bash
477	cd skills/uipath-maestro-bpmn/validator && npm install --silent
478	node validate-bpmn.mjs <file.bpmn>   # prints VALID and exits 0, or prints errors and exits 1
479	```
480	
481	`VALID` / exit 0 means the document passes all rules. Any other output lists the
482	blocking errors (gateway/condition, fake-join, superfluous-gateway, error
483	end/boundary event, timer-duration, single-blank-start, variable-reference, and
484	IS-connector checks). See [validator/README.md](../validator/README.md).
485	
486	If Node is unavailable, fall back to a well-formed-XML parse plus the structural
487	checklist below — it mirrors the same blocking rules:
488	
489	```bash
490	python3 -c "import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET; ET.parse('<file.bpmn>')"
491	```
492	
493	Then walk the structural checklist:
494	
495	1. Root is `<…:definitions>` with the BPMN + `uipath` namespaces.
496	2. Exactly one `<bpmndi:BPMNDiagram>` with a shape per node and an edge per flow.
497	3. Every `sourceRef`/`targetRef`/`attachedToRef`/`*Ref` resolves to a declared id.
498	4. Each XOR gateway: non-default flows have conditions; exactly one default.
499	5. No activity/event has more than one incoming flow.
500	6. Each event subprocess has exactly one start event, and it carries an event
501	   definition (with `isInterrupting`).
502	7. Every `vars.<id>` reference resolves to a declared variable.
503	8. Each `uipath:*` payload was produced from a `registry get` template, not
504	   hand-written.
505

1	# Registry workflow
2	
3	Every `uipath:*` payload in a Maestro `.bpmn` comes from the registry — never
4	from prose, never hand-written. This file is the loop for turning user intent
5	into registry-backed XML.
6	
7	## 1. Sync and discover
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro bpmn registry pull            # sync + cache (login for connectors/processes)
11	uip maestro bpmn registry list --limit -1 --output json   # all extension types
12	uip maestro bpmn registry search <keyword> --output json  # find a type by intent
13	uip is connections list --all-folders --output json   # live IS connections (all folders)
14	```
15	
16	Map the user's intent to an extension type from the list. Confirm the choice
17	with the user (and the specific connection / process / queue) before authoring.
18	**Never fabricate an identifier** — see [cli-conventions.md](cli-conventions.md).
19	
20	**Connection discovery must be exhaustive.** Always pass `--all-folders` to
21	`uip is connections list` — connections live in many folders and a folder-scoped
22	listing silently misses them. An empty or unmatched result from a missing
23	`--all-folders`, or from a connector key guessed from a brand name rather than
24	found via `registry search`, is a **false negative** — never conclude "no
25	connection exists" or ask the user to create one until you have searched the
26	registry for the real connector key and listed across all folders.
27	
28	`registry list` returns three buckets in `Data`: `ExtensionTypes` (the OOTB
29	extension types, always available), `Connectors` and `Processes` (only after
30	`uip login`). Each extension-type row carries `ExtensionType`, `Label`,
31	`BpmnElement` (the host BPMN element), `ExtensionTag`, and
32	`RequiresDiscovery` (`Yes` means you must resolve a concrete resource — process,
33	queue, connection — before the node is runnable).
34	
35	## 2. Get the template for each chosen type
36	
37	```bash
38	uip maestro bpmn registry get <extensionType> --output json
39	```
40	
41	`Data.ExtensionType` contains everything needed to author the node:
42	
43	| Field | Use |
44	| --- | --- |
45	| `xmlTemplate` | The literal node XML with `{placeholder}` slots. **Author from this; fill placeholders only.** |
46	| `bpmnElement` | The host BPMN element the template uses (e.g. `bpmn:ServiceTask`). |
47	| `extensionTag` | `uipath:activity`, `uipath:event`, or `uipath:mapping`. |
48	| `contextFields[]` | The `uipath:context` inputs; each may carry its own `bindingInfo`. |
49	| `bindingInfo` | How the node binds to a resource (see §4). |
50	| `inputPattern` / `inputName` / `inputTarget` | How the request body input is shaped. |
51	| `requiresDiscovery` / `isDynamic` | Whether a concrete resource must be resolved first. |
52	
53	The placeholders you fill are the obvious ones: `{id}`, `{name}`,
54	`{incomingEdge}`, `{outgoingEdge}`, `{varId}` (the output variable id), plus the
55	per-context-field placeholders (`{releaseKey}`, `{queueName}`, `{appId}`, …) and
56	the body CDATA. Leave the structural placeholders (`{incomingEdge}` /
57	`{outgoingEdge}`) wired to the sequence-flow ids you create in
58	[structural-bpmn.md](structural-bpmn.md).
59	
60	## 3. Connector (`Intsvc.*`) enrichment
61	
62	For connector types (`requiresDiscovery: Yes`, e.g.
63	`Intsvc.ActivityExecution`, `Intsvc.WaitForEvent`, `Intsvc.EventTrigger`),
64	resolve a live connection and object, then enrich:
65	
66	```bash
67	uip is connections list --all-folders --output json   # pick a connection id + its connector (search all folders)
68	uip maestro bpmn registry get Intsvc.ActivityExecution \
69	    --connection-id <id> --object-name <object> --output json
70	```
71	
72	The response adds an `ISEnrichment` block with the live field metadata. Write
73	the activity's `body` input (`target="body"`) and `context` (`connectorKey`,
74	`objectName`) from that enrichment — do not hand-author connector schemas. The
75	connection is referenced through a connection binding, `=bindings.<bindingId>`
76	(see §4).
77	
78	## 4. Bindings — from `bindingInfo`, never invented
79	
80	A node that targets a cloud resource carries a binding. The `bindingInfo` on the
81	extension type tells you the binding shape; the concrete value comes from
82	discovery or the user.
83	
84	- **Resource bindings** (`bindingInfo.resource` = `process` / `queue` /
85	  `businessRule`): the context field named by `bindingInfo.contextField`
86	  (e.g. `releaseKey`, `queueName`) holds the resource key
87	  (`bindingInfo.propertyAttribute`, usually `Key`). Resolve the real key with
88	  `registry search` / discovered `Processes` / `Queues`; never guess a GUID.
89	- **Connection bindings** (`Intsvc.*`): the context references a connection via
90	  `=bindings.<bindingId>`, and a `<uipath:binding>` of `resource="Connection"`
91	  with `propertyAttribute="ConnectionId"` in the process-level
92	  `<uipath:bindings>` holds the live connection id from `uip is connections list`.
93	
94	Declare all bindings in a single process-level `<uipath:bindings version="v1">`
95	block. Each `<uipath:binding>` carries `id`, `resource`, `propertyAttribute`,
96	and a `default` value (the resolved key/id).
97	
98	## Agent wrapper selection — pick by `processType`, not the label
99	
100	When a node invokes an agent, choose the wrapper by the resource's
101	**`processType`** (from `uip or processes list --all-fields`), not its display
102	label:
103	
104	- Coded Python agents publish as `processType: "Function"` — use the
105	  `Orchestrator.StartJob` process contract, **not** `StartAgentJob`.
106	- Agent Builder (low-code) publishes as `processType: "Agent"` →
107	  `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob`.
108	- External A2A agent addressed by URL / skillId → `A2A.AgentExecution`.
109	- Integration Service external agent → `Intsvc.*AgentExecution`.
110	
111	Gotcha: `A2A.AgentExecution` renders as an external A2A node and **disables the
112	Action dropdown** in Studio Web. Do not use it for a folder-deployed agent — the
113	canvas treats the task as misconfigured. Use `StartAgentJob`/`StartJob` for
114	folder-deployed resources.
115	
116	## API workflow — wait vs fire-and-forget
117	
118	Pick the wrapper by whether downstream needs the invocation result:
119	`Orchestrator.ExecuteApiWorkflow` **waits** for completion (result available to
120	later nodes); `Orchestrator.ExecuteApiWorkflowAsync` **returns immediately**
121	(fire-and-forget). Both are `bpmn:serviceTask` activities. Resolve `ReleaseKey`
122	(process GUID), `FolderKey`/`FolderPath`, and the request/response schemas before
123	the node is runnable — make the wait-versus-async choice explicit in the model.
124	
125	## Integration Service triggers — bind trigger properties via the CLI
126	
127	`Intsvc.TimerTrigger` and `Intsvc.EventTrigger` (and connector waits like
128	`Intsvc.WaitForEvent`) need their **trigger properties** enriched/bound through
129	the CLI — the same enrichment path as `Intsvc.*` activities (§3). A hand-authored
130	trigger shell stays **draft** until the CLI supplies the concrete trigger
131	properties, connection binding, and schemas.
132	
133	## Connectionless vs connector HTTP
134	
135	- **Connector activity** (`Intsvc.ActivityExecution` / a connector-authenticated
136	  operation): use when the call goes through a tenant connection, a dynamic
137	  connector schema, or a connector object operation. Keep the node **draft**
138	  until enriched. The CLI-owned enrichment blockers — the ones that must be
139	  resolved before upload or run, and that boundary notes should name explicitly
140	  — are **connection binding**, **dynamic schemas**, generated **package
141	  metadata** (`bindings_v2.json`, `entry-points.json`, `operate.json`,
142	  `package-descriptor.json`). Do not hand-author any of these (§3).
143	- **Connectionless / manual HTTP** (`Intsvc.HttpExecution`, or
144	  `Intsvc.UnifiedHttpRequest` when current tooling exposes the unified shape):
145	  use when the workflow itself owns the URL, method, payload, and response
146	  parsing (no connection). Author `mode="manual"`, `method`, `url`, `headers`,
147	  `parameters`, `body` directly from the registry template.
148	
149	Status vocabulary for an IS node in a summary: **executable** (activity, inputs,
150	output variable, and downstream mappings present, runtime-verified if a run was
151	done), **draft** (BPMN shape/intent present but enrichment missing), **mock**
152	(returns fixed sample data instead of calling out), **blocked** (a required URL,
153	auth, schema, or enrichment decision is missing).
154	
155	## 5. Assemble
156	
157	1. Build the document scaffold and process (see
158	   [structural-bpmn.md](structural-bpmn.md)).
159	2. Declare root variables (`BPMN.Variables` template) and the
160	   `<uipath:bindings>` block.
161	3. For each node, paste its `registry get` `xmlTemplate`, fill placeholders, and
162	   wire `{incomingEdge}`/`{outgoingEdge}` to your sequence flows.
163	4. Author the structural BPMN the registry does not emit: sequence flows,
164	   gateway conditions/defaults, event definitions, boundary events,
165	   subprocess/call-activity containers, multi-instance markers.
166	5. Generate the `bpmndi:BPMNDiagram` (shape per node, edge per flow).
167	6. Validate (see [structural-bpmn.md#validation](structural-bpmn.md#validation)).
168	
169	## OOTB extension types (29, login-free)
170	
171	These are the built-in types `registry pull` returns without login. Discover the
172	exact template for any of them with `registry get <type>`.
173	
174	| Extension type | Host element | Tag |
175	| --- | --- | --- |
176	| `Actions.HITL` | `bpmn:UserTask` | activity |
177	| `Orchestrator.StartJob` | `bpmn:ServiceTask` | activity |
178	| `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob` | `bpmn:ServiceTask` | activity |
179	| `Orchestrator.BusinessRules` | `bpmn:BusinessRuleTask` | activity |
180	| `Orchestrator.ExecuteApiWorkflowAsync` | `bpmn:ServiceTask` | activity |
181	| `Orchestrator.CreateQueueItem` | `bpmn:SendTask` | activity |
182	| `Orchestrator.CreateAndWaitForQueueItem` | `bpmn:ServiceTask` | activity |
183	| `Orchestrator.StartAgenticProcess[Async]` | `bpmn:CallActivity` | activity |
184	| `Orchestrator.StartCaseMgmtProcess[Async]` | `bpmn:CallActivity` | activity |
185	| `Intsvc.ActivityExecution` | `bpmn:SendTask` | event/activity |
186	| `Intsvc.HttpExecution` / `Intsvc.UnifiedHttpRequest` | `bpmn:SendTask` | activity |
187	| `Intsvc.WaitForEvent` | `bpmn:ReceiveTask` | event |
188	| `Intsvc.EventTrigger` | `bpmn:StartEvent` | event |
189	| `Intsvc.TimerTrigger` | `bpmn:StartEvent` | activity |
190	| `Intsvc.{Async,SyncAgent,AsyncAgent,SyncWorkflow,AsyncWorkflow}Execution` | `bpmn:ServiceTask` | activity |
191	| `A2A.AgentExecution` | `bpmn:ServiceTask` | activity |
192	| `BPMN.Variables` | `bpmn:Task` | mapping |
193	| `BPMN.ScriptTask` | `bpmn:ScriptTask` | mapping |
194	| `Maestro.ReceiveMessageEvent` | `bpmn:IntermediateCatchEvent` | event |
195	| `Maestro.SendMessageEvent` | `bpmn:IntermediateThrowEvent` | event |
196	| `Maestro.CaseRulesEvaluator` / `Maestro.CaseManagerGuardrails` | `bpmn:ServiceTask` | activity |
197	
198	This table is a discovery aid, not a substitute for `registry get` — always pull
199	the live template before authoring.

1	# Project Layout
2	
3	Maestro BPMN Process Orchestration projects use BPMN XML as source and generated JSON files as package/runtime metadata.
4	
5	## Canonical source files
6	
7	- `<project>.bpmn` - BPMN process source and UiPath extension XML. For a new
8	  project, keep the BPMN source basename exactly aligned with the project
9	  directory/name. For example, `InvoiceTriageBpmn/InvoiceTriageBpmn.bpmn`, not
10	  `InvoiceTriageBpmn/invoice-triage-bpmn.bpmn`.
11	- `project.uiproj` - UiPath project metadata. Keep it in the same project
12	  directory as the main BPMN file: `InvoiceTriageBpmn/project.uiproj`, not next
13	  to the project directory.
14	
15	For a new local project, place source files under a single project directory.
16	`uip maestro bpmn init <ProjectName> --output json` nests that directory inside
17	a solution. Inside a solution it registers the project with the parent `.uipx`;
18	outside any solution it auto-scaffolds `<ProjectName>Solution/` and nests the
19	project inside (the response adds `Data.AutoCreatedSolution` =
20	`{ Name, Path, SolutionFile }` and reports `SolutionRegistration.Status:
21	Registered`; re-running is idempotent and reports `AlreadyRegistered`):
22	
23	```text
24	ProjectNameSolution/             ← auto-scaffolded when init runs outside a solution
25	  ProjectNameSolution.uipx
26	  ProjectName/
27	    ProjectName.bpmn
28	    project.uiproj
29	```
30	
31	With `--skip-solution-registration`, the project lands bare instead, with no
32	solution wrapper:
33	
34	```text
35	ProjectName/
36	  ProjectName.bpmn
37	  project.uiproj
38	```
39	
40	If a **non-empty** directory already exists at the path you typed, init warns
41	and leaves it untouched — the project still lands in
42	`<ProjectName>Solution/<ProjectName>/`, not the existing directory.
43	
44	## Generated or CLI-managed package files
45	
46	- `bindings_v2.json` - resource bindings generated or enriched from BPMN and registry/connection metadata.
47	- `entry-points.json` - runnable start-event entry points and input/output schemas.
48	- `operate.json` - runtime/package metadata.
49	- `package-descriptor.json` - package manifest mapping generated files and BPMN content.
50	
51	Treat these JSON files as derived unless a CLI contract explicitly identifies a field as user-authored. For source fixes, edit BPMN or rerun CLI enrichment rather than patching generated output by hand.
52	
53	Local packaging requires the generated metadata set to exist. In particular,
54	`uip maestro bpmn pack <project-path> <OutputDir> --output json` consumes
55	`package-descriptor.json`; it does not create a missing descriptor from only
56	the BPMN and `project.uiproj`.
57	
58	For the regeneration and drift-check contract, see [local-metadata-regeneration-guide.md](local-metadata-regeneration-guide.md).
59	
60	## Package content
61	
62	A Process Orchestration package content folder contains:
63	
64	- One or more `.bpmn` files.
65	- `bindings_v2.json`.
66	- `entry-points.json`.
67	- `operate.json`.
68	- `package-descriptor.json`.
69	
70	The package descriptor maps BPMN and generated JSON files under `content/`. The entry point file path references the BPMN file and start event, using the root start event's unique entry point ID.
71	
72	## Authoring boundary
73	
74	Authoring owns local files and local validation. It can create or edit BPMN source, preserve existing generated files for comparison, and run validation/generation commands. It stops before upload, debug, publish, or run unless the user explicitly consents.
75	
76	Operate owns cloud-side side effects: upload, publish, deploy, debug, process run, instance lifecycle, and cloud resource refresh.
77	
78	Diagnose owns post-run inspection: incidents, variables, element executions, deployed assets, traces, and correlation back to BPMN element IDs.
